dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts participating foreign government partners, U.S. technology providers, and federal personnel involved in the program.
dimensions.evidence: To incentivize, streamline, and sustain United States foreign government partner procurement of United States-origin cyber and digital technologies.

dimensions.assessment: Provides significant strategic and financial support for technology acquisition and supply chain security for allies.
dimensions.evidence: To establish long-term cyber and digital technology procurement pipelines with United States providers

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes the appropriation of $500,000,000 from fiscal year 2026 through fiscal year 2031 plus $2,000,000 for administrative implementation.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated $500,000,000 for fiscal year 2026 through fiscal year 2031

dimensions.assessment: Creates a new procurement program within the Department of State along with interagency coordination and reporting mandates.
dimensions.evidence: There is established in the Department of State the United States Cyber and Digital Technology Procurement Program

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations through fiscal year 2031 with a statutory sunset terminating authorities eight years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The Program and its associated authorities established under this section shall terminate on the date that is eight years after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific foreign partner countries that will participate are not named in the text.
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a multi-year federal procurement support program with $500 million in authorized appropriations to assist foreign government partners in acquiring U.S. cyber and digital technologies.
